qe66729e4.question: The specific markdown->HTML rendering approach inside the JCEF view (a bundled JS renderer loaded into the browser vs a Kotlin markdown->HTML pass before load) is deferred to the plan/build; either keeps renderedMarkdown as the daemon-provided source of truth and authors no second copy.
qe66729e4.rationale: User's explicit in-chat decision. Ship a vendored markdown renderer (marked/markdown-it) as a plugin resource, load it into the JCEF page, and pass the raw daemon-provided renderedMarkdown across the Kotlin->JS bridge for client-side rendering. renderedMarkdown remains the single source of truth (no second copy authored). Keeps rendering + the later inline-comment/anchor layer (s3) in one JS layer. CSP/offline note for the build: the renderer must be a bundled local resource (no CDN), rendered read-only.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Thin three-layer review surface over existing daemon capability; reasoning stays daemon-side (k1), the plugin only renders and transports.

boundary.internal: Private to s2: the JCEF browser lifecycle, the JBCefApp.isSupported() gate, the HTML rendering of renderedMarkdown, and the read-only native-editor fallback.

ownedContracts.name: ArtifactReviewView
ownedContracts.purpose: The read-only view a reviewer sees: the artifact's own rendered content, its open questions, and whether it is currently approvable.
ownedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface OpenQuestionRef { readonly id: string; readonly text: string; readonly status: 'open'|'resolved'|'ignored'|'deferred'; }
interface ArtifactReviewView { readonly artifactId: string; readonly kind: string; readonly renderedMarkdown: string; readonly openQuestions: readonly OpenQuestionRef[]; readonly approvable: boolean; readonly blockReason?: string | null; }

consumedContracts.name: PendingArtifactList
consumedContracts.purpose: The typed descriptor of a pending-approval artifact + the read that enumerates them; S002 keys the content fetch off its mdPath.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A — Discover, read, and approve (minimal review loop)

api.name: workflow.artifactContent
api.signature: 'workflow.artifactContent': (params: { repo?: string; mdPath: string }) => Promise<ArtifactReviewView | { error: string }>

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: Open project's absolute root; falls back to process.env.INSRC_REPO like the sibling workflow.pending / workflow.approve handlers.

parameters.name: mdPath
parameters.purpose: The rendered .md path from the selected S001 PendingArtifact.mdPath; validated to resolve under the repo's docs/ tree (path-traversal guard) before reading.

returns.meaning: On success the full sc2 review view (renderedMarkdown from the .md + openQuestions/approvable/blockReason from the sibling .json meta). On repo-unresolved / path-invalid / unreadable, a structured { error }, mirroring workflow.pending so the client maps it to Unavailable.

errors.condition: repo cannot be resolved (no param, no INSRC_REPO), or mdPath is empty / does not resolve under the repo's docs/ tree / is not a recognized workflow artifact .md.
the .md is unreadable, or its sibling .insrc/artifacts/<KIND>-<hash>.json (via jsonPathForMd) is missing/malformed.

preconditions: The selected artifact came from the S001 workflow.pending list (mdPath is a descriptor field), so it names a rendered workflow artifact under docs/.
postconditions: No file is written or mutated (read-only).
renderedMarkdown is the .md read verbatim — no transformation, no divergent second copy (k5/lc1/ac3).

api.name: handleArtifactContent
api.signature: handleArtifactContent(params: { repo?: string; mdPath?: string }, repoEnv: string | undefined): ArtifactReviewView | { error: string }

parameters.name: params
parameters.purpose: The IPC params; repo/mdPath resolution + validation live here (pure), mirroring S001's handleWorkflowPending so the contract is integration-testable without booting the daemon.

parameters.name: repoEnv
parameters.purpose: The INSRC_REPO fallback the daemon handler passes (process.env['INSRC_REPO']).

returns.meaning: The pure core the handler delegates to: resolve+validate repo/mdPath, read the .md + sibling .json, assemble the view, and map every failure to a structured { error }.

errors.condition: same repo-unresolved / path-invalid / unreadable conditions; never throws for these — returns { error }.

api.name: jsonPathForMd

parameters.name: mdPath
parameters.purpose: The rendered artifact .md path; mapped to its hash-flat .insrc/artifacts/<KIND>-<hash>.json via the in-file insrc:artifact marker to read the meta.

returns.meaning: The sibling .json path holding the artifact meta/body (existing helper, gates.ts:758 — consumed unchanged).

errors.condition: the .md has no insrc:artifact marker or an unknown extension (existing throw; the handler catches it and returns { error }).

preconditions: mdPath is a nested workflow artifact .md carrying the insrc:artifact marker.
postconditions: Pure; no I/O beyond reading the marker.

api.name: DaemonGateway.artifactReviewView
api.signature: fun artifactReviewView(projectRootPath: String, mdPath: String): ArtifactContentResult

parameters.name: projectRootPath
parameters.purpose: The open project's root (the repo arg every gateway call carries, k3-scoping).

parameters.name: mdPath
parameters.purpose: The selected PendingArtifactDto's mdPath, forwarded to the daemon.

returns.meaning: Loaded(view) on ok; Unavailable(reason) on ok=false / DaemonUnavailableException / unexpected fault — mirroring S001's PendingQueryResult so a fetch error never renders as blank/empty content.

errors.condition: daemon returns a structured error, the socket is unreachable, or the reply is malformed (no throw escapes).

preconditions: Reaches the daemon only over the existing DaemonGateway.call('workflow.artifactContent', {repo, mdPath}) transport (k2).
postconditions: Forwards the daemon's view verbatim (no client-side classification — k1).

api.name: JBCefApp.isSupported

returns.meaning: IntelliJ-Platform gate (external, consumed): true selects the JBCefBrowser HTML render; false selects the read-only native-editor fallback carrying the same review actions (ac2/lc2/k6).

preconditions: Called on the EDT at content-view open time.

dataModelChanges.details: The sc2 contract realized as an internal-shared type (TS in the daemon, mirrored as a Kotlin data class in the plugin): { artifactId; kind; renderedMarkdown; openQuestions: OpenQuestionRef[]; approvable; blockReason? }. renderedMarkdown is the .md read verbatim (k5/lc1); approvable/blockReason derive from the .json meta.review block-verdict. Produced only by s2; consumed by s3/s4/s5.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: + interface ArtifactReviewView { artifactId; kind; renderedMarkdown; openQuestions; approvable; blockReason? }

dataModelChanges.details: The sc2 open-question projection { id; text; status: 'open'|'resolved'|'ignored'|'deferred' }, read from the artifact .json body/openQuestions. S002 surfaces them read-only; recording resolutions is s4.
Plugin sealed result mirroring S001's PendingQueryResult: Loaded(view) | Unavailable(reason). Keeps a fetch error DISTINCT from an empty/blank view.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: S002 owns sc2 and realizes it via the workflow.artifactContent handler (+ pure handleArtifactContent) that assembles ArtifactReviewView (renderedMarkdown from the .md, openQuestions + approvable/blockReason from the sibling .json via jsonPathForMd), mirrored as Kotlin types in the plugin. The sc2 interface is kept EXACTLY as sketched (renderedMarkdown unchanged) so s3/s4/s5 consume it unaltered — the artifact.get correction is realized by a new handler, not a contract change, so no HLD amendment is needed.

The content view opens from a selected S001 PendingArtifact; S002 keys the fetch off that descriptor's mdPath (and artifactId/kind for the header). It does NOT re-run or re-implement the pending scan (s1's boundary).

errorCases.scenario: The client-supplied mdPath escapes the repo ('..' traversal / absolute outside repo / not under docs/).
errorCases.detection: handleArtifactContent normalizes mdPath to an absolute real path and checks containment within join(repo,'docs') before any read.
errorCases.response: Return { error } naming the invalid path; perform no read.
errorCases.userImpact: Content pane shows 'content unavailable'; nothing outside the workspace is read.

errorCases.scenario: The artifact .md no longer exists or is unreadable (approved/rejected/moved between poll and open).
errorCases.detection: readFileSync(mdPath) throws ENOENT/EACCES, caught in handleArtifactContent.
errorCases.response: Return { error } with the read failure reason.
errorCases.userImpact: Explicit 'content unavailable' (not a blank pane); resolves after the list refreshes.

errorCases.scenario: The sibling meta .json is missing or malformed.
errorCases.detection: jsonPathForMd throws (no marker/unknown extension) or JSON.parse of the resolved .json throws — both caught.
errorCases.response: Return { error } rather than a half-assembled view.
errorCases.userImpact: Told the metadata is unreadable instead of a misleading approvable state.

errorCases.scenario: repo unresolved (no param + no INSRC_REPO), or mdPath empty.
errorCases.detection: handleArtifactContent non-empty guards at entry, mirroring handleWorkflowPending.
errorCases.response: Return { error }; never a partial success.
errorCases.userImpact: 'content unavailable'; an unresolvable list entry cannot be opened.

errorCases.scenario: Daemon socket unreachable, or a structured error / malformed reply during the fetch.
errorCases.detection: DaemonGateway.artifactReviewView catches DaemonUnavailableException + RuntimeException and maps a daemon ok=false via UnixSocketDaemonRpc.parse result.error framing.
errorCases.response: Return ArtifactContentResult.Unavailable(reason); no throw escapes onto the EDT/poll thread.
errorCases.userImpact: 'insrc backing service unavailable — <reason>', distinct from an empty artifact.

edgeCases.expected: Not an error: degrade to the read-only native-editor fallback showing the same renderedMarkdown with the same review actions (ac2/lc2/k6).

edgeCases.input: The artifact was approved/rejected between list refresh and open.
edgeCases.expected: The .md still renders read-only; approvable reflects the CURRENT meta (false once approved).
View renders with no questions section — not an error.
approvable=false + blockReason carried for s5; s2 renders content and surfaces the reason read-only.
JCEF renders it (O(size)); the fetch is a single on-open request/reply, not a poll (k7 unaffected).

invariantsToPreserve.text: The artifact's own .md is the single source of truth: renderedMarkdown is the file read verbatim, no divergent second copy (k5/lc1/ac3).
The plugin stays a thin orchestrator: the daemon owns the read + view assembly; the plugin only renders + transports (k1).
All daemon access stays over the existing local Unix-domain-socket JSON-RPC channel; the plugin never reads workflow files/DB directly (k2).
The one plugin artifact loads across all four IDEs off the shared platform module and degrades gracefully where the embedded browser is unavailable (k6/lc2).

migration.stateBefore: S001 (main fabe840) ships the review tool window with the pending LIST only: daemon workflow.pending (+ handleWorkflowPending) returns PendingArtifact incl. mdPath; plugin DaemonGateway.pendingArtifacts + PendingQueryResult over UnixSocketDaemonRpc (parse surfaces structured result.error as ok=false); ReviewToolWindow/ReviewPanel renders the list via ReviewListViews. No IPC serves a workflow .md (artifact.get resolves the LanceDB skill store); no content view. resolveArtifactMdPath/jsonPathForMd/artifactJsonPath already map identity<->.md/.json.
migration.stateAfter: Daemon adds workflow.artifactContent (+ handleArtifactContent) assembling the sc2 ArtifactReviewView, path-guarded under docs/. Plugin adds ArtifactReviewView/OpenQuestionRef types, ArtifactContentResult, a DaemonGateway.artifactReviewView wrapper, and a content view in the existing ReviewToolWindow (JCEF HTML when supported, else read-only native fallback). All S001 behaviour unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add daemon types (ArtifactReviewView, OpenQuestionRef) + pure handleArtifactContent (docs/ containment guard, .md verbatim read, sibling .json via jsonPathForMd, failures -> { error }). Net-new module.
Register workflow.artifactContent in src/daemon/index.ts (beside workflow.pending), delegating to handleArtifactContent with INSRC_REPO fallback. Net-new method key.

Add plugin types (ArtifactReviewView/OpenQuestionRef data classes, ArtifactContentResult sealed) + DaemonGateway.artifactReviewView wrapper over call() (ok->Loaded, ok=false/DaemonUnavailable/RuntimeException->Unavailable), wired through DaemonGatewayService. Additive to the S001 interface.

Add the content view to ReviewToolWindow: a pending-list selection triggers a bounded on-demand fetch via artifactReviewView; render renderedMarkdown->HTML in JBCefBrowser when JBCefApp.isSupported(), else the native-editor fallback; distinct 'content unavailable' state on Unavailable. Extract pure ArtifactContentViews + renderModeFor(jcefSupported).
Add tests (daemon node:test for handleArtifactContent + the handler; plugin JUnit for artifactReviewView, real parse framing, ArtifactContentViews, renderModeFor). Verify locally.

migration.backwardCompat: Fully backward compatible: workflow.artifactContent is a NET-NEW IPC method key — no existing handler changes. The plugin change is additive; the S001 pending list is untouched. An older daemon without the handler returns a top-level 'unknown method' error, which the S001-hardened UnixSocketDaemonRpc.parse maps to ok=false -> the plugin shows 'content unavailable' (graceful degradation). No public/cross-repo IPC contract is broken.

alternativesConsidered.name: Daemon read handler returns the full ArtifactReviewView (markdown); plugin renders HTML client-side
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A thin new daemon read IPC assembles sc2 ArtifactReviewView (renderedMarkdown from the .md + openQuestions/approvable/blockReason from the .json meta); the plugin converts markdown->HTML inside JCEF, native-editor fallback shows the same markdown.
alternativesConsidered.approach: New thin daemon read handler keyed by the S001 pending identity (mdPath validated under docs/) returns the full sc2 view (renderedMarkdown verbatim + meta-derived fields via jsonPathForMd); the plugin adds a DaemonGateway wrapper + a content view that renders HTML in JBCefBrowser when JBCefApp.isSupported(), else a read-only native-editor fallback. No second copy is stored.
pros: One daemon read produces the whole review view for s3/s4/s5.
Reuses the proven path helpers + the S001 transport/framing.
cons: The plugin needs a markdown->HTML renderer in JCEF.
The daemon must path-guard the client-supplied mdPath.

alternativesConsidered.name: Daemon renders markdown->HTML server-side; plugin just loads the HTML
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The new read handler returns pre-rendered HTML; the plugin loads it into JCEF, fallback shows raw markdown.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same view assembly but the daemon converts .md->HTML and the sc2 view carries html; the plugin loads it directly.
cons: Re-shapes the owned sc2 contract (html vs renderedMarkdown) that s3/s4/s5 depend on.
Adds a markdown->HTML dependency to the daemon.
Derived HTML can drift from the canonical .md (borderline lc1).
S003's DOM-anchored comments are harder over opaque daemon HTML.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates sc2 (re-shapes the shared contract s3/s4/s5 consume) and is partial on ac3/k5 (a server-rendered HTML copy can drift from the .md); adds a daemon rendering dependency for a purely presentational concern. Centralized rendering is not worth re-opening the owned contract.

alternativesConsidered.name: Plugin reads the mdPath file directly (no new IPC)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The plugin opens the S001 descriptor's mdPath from disk itself and reads the sibling .json — zero daemon change.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Skip a new IPC: the plugin reads mdPath (and the sibling .json) from disk directly and renders in JCEF with the native fallback.
cons: Violates k1 + the daemon-owns-access architecture rule.
mdPath is best-effort, forcing the plugin to duplicate resolveArtifactMdPath/jsonPathForMd + couple to the docs/ layout.
No daemon-side seam for future clients.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Breaks k1 and the daemon-owns-access rule (k2) by having the plugin open files + derive paths itself, and only partially satisfies sc1/sc2. The zero-daemon-change saving is not worth breaking the boundary the whole system rests on.

openQuestions: The specific markdown->HTML rendering approach inside the JCEF view (a bundled JS renderer loaded into the browser vs a Kotlin markdown->HTML pass before load) is deferred to the plan/build; either keeps renderedMarkdown as the daemon-provided source of truth and authors no second copy.
